handoff.reportSection:
## Warehouse connections

- **Supabase — needs the browser:** Setup credentials were declined. Complete the Postgres/Supabase connection at [PostHog data warehouse source setup](https://eu.posthog.com/project/201293/data-warehouse/new-source?kind=Supabase&utm_source=wizard&utm_campaign=warehouse-source). Use the public Session Pooler host, port `6543`, `postgres.<project-ref>` user, database password, and scope the import to `public`; do not sync `auth` or other internal schemas.
- **Resend — needs the browser:** Setup credentials were declined. Complete the connection at [PostHog data warehouse source setup](https://eu.posthog.com/project/201293/data-warehouse/new-source?kind=Resend&utm_source=wizard&utm_campaign=warehouse-source). Use a full-access API key with read access to emails, contacts, audiences, broadcasts, and domains.
- **OpenAI — needs the browser:** Setup credentials were declined. Complete the connection at [PostHog data warehouse source setup](https://eu.posthog.com/project/201293/data-warehouse/new-source?kind=OpenAI&utm_source=wizard&utm_campaign=warehouse-source). Use an organization Admin API key (`sk-admin…`); a project key cannot import organization usage and cost data.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog for the Vite React browser app, configure public environment keys, document them for developers, and make the existing CSP compatible with the SDK.
handoff.did: Updated `src/lib/posthog.ts` to consume `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`, initialize the existing `posthog-js` singleton only when both are present, fail loudly in development when either is absent, and remain a production no-op when unconfigured. The existing entry point (`src/main.tsx`) already calls `initPostHog()` once before rendering and passes the exported singleton to the existing React integration; later call sites should import the shared client or guarded `capture` helper from `src/lib/posthog`. Removed the email address from the existing `email_link_clicked` event properties so it does not capture PII. Updated `index.html` CSP: added `https://*.posthog.com` to `script-src` and `connect-src`, and added `worker-src 'self' blob: data:`; left `default-src`, `style-src`, `font-src`, and `img-src` unchanged. Created `.env.example` with placeholder values for `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST`. Used wizard environment tooling to set both actual values in the ignored `.env`.
handoff.forNextAgent: The PostHog client is the singleton exported by `src/lib/posthog.ts`; `src/main.tsx` invokes `initPostHog()` before React renders. Import `posthog` for SDK APIs or use the exported guarded `capture` / `captureError` helpers. Keep event names snake_case and do not put PII in event properties. CSP now permits browser SDK assets, ingestion, and replay workers via the named directives.
handoff.evidence: Read the final `src/lib/posthog.ts`, `.env.example`, and CSP section of `index.html`; `check_env_keys` confirmed `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST` are present in `.env`. No build, lint, or tests were run, per task instruction.
handoff.assumptions: The existing `src/lib/posthog.ts` and `src/main.tsx` implementation was established by an upstream workflow step; this task corrected its environment-variable convention and CSP rather than creating a parallel initialization path.

handoff.goals: Wire stable PostHog user identification at the appropriate authentication boundary so events and errors inherit the known user identity.
handoff.did: No files were changed. This is a Vite/React client-only portfolio. The only Supabase usage in the inspected source is a browser client used to invoke functions; no sign-in, registration, session retrieval, auth-state subscription, logout handler, or authenticated user model exists. The visible account panel is static portfolio-owner content, not an app user. Consequently, there is no legitimate stable user id or identity boundary at which to call `posthog.identify()`, and adding one would invent an identity contrary to the analytics contract.
handoff.forNextAgent: The existing initialized browser singleton remains anonymous by design, so its captures and `PostHogErrorBoundary` errors share the anonymous PostHog distinct id. If real visitor authentication is added later, identify only after successful login/sign-up (and once on startup when an existing session is restored) using `user.id` or another stable auth primary key; place email/name only in identify person properties, call `posthog.reset()` on logout, and reset before a direct account switch. Do not identify the static portfolio owner or use contact-form input as an identity.
handoff.evidence: Read the JavaScript web commandments and identify skill. Inspected `src/lib/posthog.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/components/panels/AccountPanel.tsx`, `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts`, and `src/hooks/useAnalytics.ts`; searched the source for Supabase auth/session/login/logout/user flows. No auth flow or non-static user identifier was found.
handoff.assumptions: Supabase Edge Functions and any server-side implementation are not included in this project directory; based on the available browser source, they do not provide a frontend auth boundary.

handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught browser errors reach PostHog through the JavaScript SDK's supported global mechanism, without adding scattered manual error capture.
handoff.did: Updated `src/lib/posthog.ts` in the shared, one-time `posthog.init()` configuration to enable PostHog exception autocapture for unhandled browser errors and unhandled promise rejections. Explicitly set `capture_console_errors: false` so noisy console output is not intentionally ingested. The existing root-level `PostHogErrorBoundary` in `src/main.tsx` remains in place for React render errors, providing framework-level coverage alongside SDK global exception autocapture.
handoff.forNextAgent: No dependencies were installed and no build, lint, or tests were run, per this instrument-only task. The initialization singleton now globally handles browser uncaught errors/rejections; the existing React boundary handles render crashes. Production source-map upload should be handled in the deployment/release workflow if readable production stack traces are required.
handoff.evidence: Read the mandated framework rules and error-tracking references, confirmed the existing root `PostHogErrorBoundary` and singleton initialization, then successfully applied the targeted `capture_exceptions` configuration edit. No verification commands were run by instruction.
handoff.assumptions: `posthog-js` default bundle supports exception autocapture, consistent with the installed `posthog-js` dependency and SDK reference. Existing React error boundary was established upstream and intentionally preserved.

handoff.goals: Install the declared PostHog dependency, verify the project build and lint scripts, and strictly review the upstream PostHog changeset across minimality, unrelated changes, codebase patterns, framework example shape, runtime wiring, and CSP correctness.
handoff.did: Reviewed every upstream changeset file plus the changed initialization caller and one neighboring analytics pattern. Applied 2 fixes: (1) Minimal — simplified `src/lib/posthog.ts` by removing redundant explicit defaults/session-recording settings, a development-only global/debug `loaded` callback, and narration comments while retaining guarded one-time initialization, default data capture, outbound tracking, and explicit exception autocapture; (2) Codebase patterns — aligned the PostHog additions in `src/main.tsx` with that file's existing single-quote/no-semicolon style and removed a redundant JSX narration comment. Unrelated passed with no fix; Example shapes passed with initialization still early, singleton-based, environment-backed, and recognizable as the framework pattern. Verified CSP directive-by-directive: PostHog subdomains are permitted by `script-src` and `connect-src`, while `worker-src` permits `blob:`. Preserved all event names, properties, and firing locations. Confirmed the real Vite key and host variables are present in `.env`. Installation and command verification were attempted using detected-primary Bun, but the runtime lacks the Bun executable: `bun add posthog-js`, `bun run build`, and `bun run lint` all exited 127 with `bun: command not found`. Per the workflow, did not retry installation through a secondary package manager.
handoff.forNextAgent: The integration review is complete with 2 fixes. The code-level review dimensions all pass, but this environment could not install or compile because Bun is unavailable. In an environment with Bun, run `bun install` (or otherwise install the already-declared manifest dependencies according to project policy), then `bun run build` and `bun run lint`.
